comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C2, C17, C18, C64-C70 regarding experimental design, sample collection, and QC procedures. Both evaluations rate the dataset and methods as SUPPORTED with solid evidence. OpenEval provides more technical detail on QC thresholds while peer reviewers emphasize the resource value.

Perfect agreement on claims C19-C24 regarding cell type identification using marker genes. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on the appropriateness of marker-based annotation, while peer reviewers note that initial concerns about cell classification were resolved during revision.

Perfect agreement on claims C3, C25-C30 regarding temporal emergence of neuronal subtypes. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and acknowledge this corroborates established knowledge about deep-layer neurons preceding upper-layer neurons in primate neurogenesis.

Perfect agreement on claims C46-C51 regarding cross-species comparative analysis. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and affirm findings of conserved neurogenic processes with primate-specific oRG expansion. Both note the value for future comparative studies.

Perfect agreement on claims C52-C55 regarding transcription factor analysis using SCENIC. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and acknowledge both conserved TF expression and divergent regulatory networks between macaque and mouse as intriguing findings.

Perfect agreement on claim C63 regarding technical limitations of cell capture efficiency. Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN, noting this is acknowledged as a limitation but lacks quantitative validation. Peer reviewers note methodological concerns were partially addressed in revision.

Strong agreement on claims C1, C6-C16, C56-C60, C62 regarding background context and established knowledge. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes C61 (novel candidates) while peer review excludes it, but both treat background claims as appropriately cited foundational context.

Strong agreement on claims C31-C38 regarding pseudotime analysis and novel gene identification. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes validation through known markers, while peer reviewers highlight the identification of novel receptors on oRG cells as a key strength. Peer review also includes C5 in this result.

Strong agreement on claims C4, C40-C45 regarding trajectory analysis and fate determination. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C39 as appropriately cautious hypothesis, while peer reviewers affirm the findings corroborate early progenitor specification. Both acknowledge the evidence for shared molecular temporal identities.

Disagreement on claim C5 regarding BMP, FGF, and WNT pathway differences. OpenEval rates this UNSUPPORTED, stating the finding is not substantiated in results/figures and appears to be an overclaim. Peer reviewers include C5 with other novel findings (C31-C38) and rate as SUPPORTED, though they focus more on novel receptors than specific pathway analysis.

Partial overlap on claim C39 (hypothesis about progenitor specification). OpenEval includes C39 with trajectory analysis (C4, C40-C45) and rates SUPPORTED while noting C39 is explicitly hypothetical. Peer reviewers separate C39 with C61 as UNCERTAIN speculative claims requiring future research.

Minimal overlap on claim C61 (novel candidates TMOD1, PID1, LINGO1). OpenEval includes C61 with background context and rates SUPPORTED as appropriately identified novel candidates. Peer reviewers group C61 with C39 as UNCERTAIN speculative claims presented as hypotheses for future exploration.
